text: When you wake up in the morning, tell yourself: The people I deal with today will be meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, dishonest, jealous, and surly.
Whatever this is that I am, it is flesh and a little spirit and an intelligence.
There is a limit to the time assigned you, and if you don't use it to free yourself it will be gone and never return.
Concentrate every minute like a Roman, like a man, on doing what's in front of you with precise and genuine seriousness.
Give thyself time to learn something new and good, and cease to be whirled around.
You could leave life right now. Let that determine what you do and say and think.
The longest-lived and the shortest-lived man, when they come to die, lose one and the same thing.
Remember that all is opinion.
Human life. Duration: momentary. Nature: changeable. Perception: dim.
Waste not the remnant of thy life in those imaginations touching other folk.
A man should be upright, not kept upright.
Never esteem anything as of advantage to you that will make you break your word or lose your self-respect.
Respect the faculty that forms thy judgments.
Each of us lives only now, this brief instant.
Nothing has such power to broaden the mind as the ability to investigate systematically and truly all that comes under thy observation in life.
As surgeons keep their instruments and knives always at hand for cases requiring immediate treatment, so shouldst thou have thy thoughts ready.
Nothing earthly succeeds by ignoring heaven, nothing heavenly by ignoring the earth.
By a tranquil mind I mean nothing else than a mind well ordered.
People try to get away from it all—to the country, to the beach, to the mountains. Which is idiotic: you can get away from it anytime you like. By going within.
Disturbance comes only from within—from our own perceptions.
Choose not to be harmed—and you won't feel harmed. Don't feel harmed—and you haven't been.
Whatever happens at all happens as it should; you will find this true, if you watch narrowly.
You have a mind? Well, why not use it?
Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over thee. While thou livest, while it is in thy power, be good.
Let your occupations be few, if you would lead a tranquil life.
Then what should we work for? Only this: proper understanding; unselfish action; truthful speech.
Observe always that everything is the result of a change, and get used to thinking that there is nothing Nature loves so well as to change existing forms.
Constantly regard the universe as one living being, having one substance and one soul.
At dawn, when you have trouble getting out of bed, tell yourself: I have to go to work—as a human being.
How easy it is to repel and to wipe away every impression which is troublesome or unsuitable.
A man makes no noise over a good deed, but passes on to another as a vine to bear grapes again in season.
The whole is damaged if you cut away anything—anything at all—from its continuity and its coherence.
Not to feel exasperated, or defeated, or despondent because your days aren't packed with wise and moral actions.
It is crazy to want what is impossible.
Nothing happens to anybody which he is not fitted by nature to bear.
Things have no hold on the soul. They have no access to it, cannot move or direct it.
The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
Live with the gods.
The intelligence of the universe is social.
But true good fortune is what you make for yourself.
Just that you do the right thing. The rest doesn't matter.
The best revenge is not to be like your enemy.
Return unto thyself as soon as may be, and be not out of tune longer than thou must needs.
I do what is mine to do; the rest doesn't disturb me.
Reverence the gods, and help men. Short is life.
All things are implicated with one another, and the bond is holy.
No matter what anyone says or does, my task is to be good.
Retire into thyself. The rational principle which rules has this nature, that it is content with itself when it does what is just.
Think of yourself as dead. You have lived your life. Now, take what's left and live it properly.
External things are not the problem. It's your assessment of them. Which you can erase right now.
In your actions, don't procrastinate. In your conversations, don't confuse. In your thoughts, don't wander.
Objective judgment, now, at this very moment. Unselfish action, now, at this very moment.
Today I escaped from anxiety. Or no, I discarded it, because it was within me, in my own perceptions.
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be. Be one.
To live your brief life rightly, isn't that enough?
How much more damage anger and grief do than the things that cause them.
If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
